newsitem.title: CHINA: China plans to float chemical firms abroad.
newsitem.headline: China plans to float chemical firms abroad.

text.p: China is preparing one or two companies in the chemical industry for listing on a foreign stock market, the Business Weekly said on Sunday.
It also said that one or two pilot companies would issue convertible bonds on a trial basis.
Chemical Industry Minister Gu Xiulian made the disclosures in a report in the English-language newspaper without naming any of the companies or saying which markets might be chosen.
Chinese securities regulators are known to be preparing another batch of companies for listing on markets outside the country.
Gu gave no indication of whether the chemical industry firms were likely to be among the next group to be listed or how much progress has been made on the planned share offerings.

Tianjin Bohai Chemical Group is listed in Hong Kong as well as on the Shanghai exchange while Jilin Chemical Industrial Co Ltd trades in both Hong Kong and in New York as well as on the Shenzhen bourse.
Gu said convertible bonds required legal guidelines which have not yet been set.
She also said the industry needed to raise funds to make technical upgradings and that stock and bond offerings would help reach these goals.
